snippet.text: Builder agent, 2026-11-21, item 2 of [issue #559](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/559): `melian compare export` now prints Melian's first read of each valid miss, the cause it reads from the round's own records, with the run and sighting IDs and numbers it rests on, and `melian compare stats` totals the reads once per defect. The rule for whether a lens run saw a miss's lines moved from the evals' `Miss.unscoped` to `MissLines` in `packages/pipeline/src/miss-cause.ts`, with the hunk test as core's `Revision.shows`; `Miss.unscoped` and `MissEvidence.stagesAt` now call it, their messages unchanged. `MissCause` reads the cause, and `ComparisonCauses` computes it for each attributed entry after `ComparisonReader` reads them. Nothing is stored and no version moved, as [the first-read decision](../decisions/2026-11-21-miss-cause-is-read-on-export.md) records. The change reads stored records and writes no stored shape, guards no trust, and so owes no hand mutation proof; a scratch run of 24 mutants of `miss-cause.ts` against its tests killed all 24. Two more, removing and inverting `ComparisonCauses.read`'s skip of a storage with no attributed entry, were killed too. The core modules the adjudication reaches changed, so `npm run code-hashes` recorded them again; each stored head's adjudication decides again once, with no model call.

snippet.text: **Melian's first read of each miss.** `melian compare export` prints, for each valid miss, what Melian reads as the cause from the round's own records: `not covered`, `cut short`, `never shown`, `seen, not reported`, `reported, refuted`, `reported, not matched` or `no record`. Beside it are the facts, IDs and numbers only: each covering run's lens and level, stage and conversation, how it ended, whether its prompt carried the file whole, and which of the miss's lines `read_file` delivered, then each overlapping lens claim's ID, its finding and the verifier's verdict. The markdown form adds a section after the maintainer notes, and JSON a `missCauses` map keyed by round. Each states that the read is as of that export. `melian compare stats` totals the reads once per defect. The read is computed, never stored, and is never a person's reason. [The design](../design.md#state-storage) gives the rules.

snippet.text: | `melian compare export <range\|#pr> [--out <path>] [--json]` | Prints the changeset's comparison rounds as markdown, or JSON with comparisons keyed by round ID and a separate unattributed map, author emails included, so a JSON export is not for publishing; the markdown form prints names only. Both carry Melian's first read of each valid miss, with the run and sighting IDs and numbers it rests on, computed from the round's records in the clone as the export runs and labelled as of that export: a `## Melian's first read of each miss` section in markdown, and `missCauses` in JSON. An explicit path writes the output there | `0`, `1` missing comparison or unwritable output |

snippet.text: Problem: a person's reason for a valid miss says what should have caught it, not where Melian's run lost it. Example: a Codex finding at `src/user.ts:30` is a valid miss, and the correctness lens covered the file; whether that lens was cut by its budget, never shown line 30, shown it and said nothing, or reported it and had the verifier refute it calls for four different fixes. Solution: whenever `melian compare export` or `melian compare stats` reads a comparison, Melian reads the cause of each valid miss from the round's own telemetry, its diff in the clone and its verdict, and labels it Melian's first read. The first rule that holds names it: `no record` when the clone holds no telemetry of the round's run, its commits are missing, or every lens run lacks the files its prompt carried, as an older Melian's do; `reported, refuted` when every lens claim on the miss's lines was refuted, and `reported, not matched` when any other stood; `not covered` when no lens run's coverage held the file; `seen, not reported` when a covering run's prompt carried the file's diff whole with a hunk on the lines, or `read_file` delivered it one of them; `never shown` when a covering run completed without that; and `cut short` when every covering run ended early. The export lists the facts each read rests on, as IDs and numbers, and says the read is as of that export; stats totals the reads once per defect. Nothing is stored, so a later rule rereads every miss. [The first-read decision](decisions/2026-11-21-miss-cause-is-read-on-export.md) says why.
